exercises.instruction: What was actually said in the chat? Pick the meaning.

options: As far as I know, at eight.
I know how many times at eight.
items.explanation: Kadarıyla is a caveat: “as far as I know,” not a guarantee.

options: Ece said the webinar isn't at nine.
According to Ece, the webinar is at nine.
As far as I know Ece, the webinar is at nine.
items.explanation: -dığına göre with a verb of speech is a source: “according to Ece.”

items.prompt: Herkesin «ses yok» yazdığına göre mikrofon kapalı.
options: Everyone writes that there's no mic.
As far as everyone knows, the mic is off.
Judging by everyone writing “no sound,” the mic is off.
items.say: Herkesin ses yok yazdığına göre mikrofon kapalı.
items.explanation: Fact + göre + conclusion: “judging by the fact that…”

options: As far as I can see, everyone is happy.
Everyone is happy with how much I saw.
I saw that everyone was happy.
items.explanation: Gördüğüm kadarıyla is the limit of what I see.

options: I heard the course go up in price.
Rumor has it the course will get more expensive.
As far as I've heard, there won't be a price hike.
items.explanation: Duyduğuma göre … -mış passes on a rumor: “rumor has it.”

exercises.instruction: Match the Turkish frame with the English one.

pairs.right: as far as I can see

items.explanation: Kadarıyla is the limit of your own knowledge. Göre is a source: someone's words, a rumor, something you read.

exercises.instruction: Pick the form that fits the blank.

items.text: Deniz Hoca'nın ___ göre kayıt yarın paylaşılacakmış.
items.translation: According to Deniz Hoca, the recording will be posted tomorrow.
items.explanation: Before göre comes the dative, and “she” gets an n: yazdığı + n + a.

items.translation: As far as I understand, the webinar was canceled.
items.explanation: Before kadarıyla, only the person, no dative.

items.translation: Judging by everyone being silent, the sound is gone.
items.explanation: After voiceless s comes t: sustuğu, plus n + a before göre.

items.text: Webinarın dokuzda ___ göre bir saatimiz var.
items.translation: Since the webinar starts at nine, we have an hour.
items.explanation: Future is -(y)acağına göre.

items.translation: Judging by what I read, the course will get more expensive.
items.explanation: “I” + dative: okuduğum + a.

exercises.instruction: Which frame does each sentence need?

entries.text: According to Ece, the webinar was moved.
As far as I remember, there will be a recording.
Judging by everyone being silent, the sound dropped.
As far as I understand, you're not coming.
Rumor has it the course will get more expensive.
As far as I can see, everyone is happy.

items.explanation: Other people's words, rumors and conclusions from facts take göre. “As far as I know / see / remember” takes kadarıyla.

exercises.instruction: Webinar chat: build the message from words in order.
exercises.description: A non-standard exercise: messages to the live chat under a running timer.

items.explanation: Source: Ece'nin söylediğine göre … -mış.
Limit of knowledge: bildiğim kadarıyla.
Conclusion from a fact: yazdığına göre.
Limit of understanding: anladığım kadarıyla.
Source is something read: okuduğuma göre.
Conclusion from a future fact: -acağına göre.

exercises.instruction: Final broadcast: five questions, you need four right.

items.prompt: How do you say “As far as I've heard, there will be a recording”?
items.explanation: Limit of knowledge is kadarıyla, and before it only the person: duyduğum.

items.statement: “Bildiğim kadarıyla” is a guarantee: “I know for sure.”
items.explanation: It's a caveat: “as far as I know.” Beyond that, the speaker makes no promises.

items.prompt: “According to Deniz Hoca, the course will get more expensive.” What's missing? Deniz Hoca'nın ___ göre kursa zam gelecekmiş.
items.explanation: Before göre, the dative with n: söylediğine.

items.prompt: “Since the recording came, we can watch.”
items.explanation: The fact is already there, next comes the conclusion: geldiğine göre.

items.prompt: Why is there -mış at the end of “… göre webinar dokuzdaymış”?
options: It shows the information is secondhand.
It makes the sentence a question.
It means past tense: the webinar already happened.
items.explanation: -mış marks reported speech: I didn't see it myself, someone told me.
